import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_4.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV into a dataframe
# All source tables have the same schema as the target:
# ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
# So we can union (concat) them directly.
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and in order
    df = df[['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']]
    dfs.append(df)

# Concatenate all source dataframes (union)
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# According to the target examples:
# - 'Year' is string, e.g. "1986 (59th)"
# - 'Category' is string, e.g. "Actress -- Supporting Role"
# - 'Nominee' is string
# - 'Movie' is string, sometimes with extra info in braces, e.g. "Children of a Lesser God {'Mrs. Norman'}"
# - 'Winner' is string, either "NO" or presumably "YES" (not shown but consistent with examples)

# Check and enforce dtypes as string for all columns
for col in ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']:
    target_df[col] = target_df[col].astype(str)

# The prompt does not specify any transformation on the content of columns,
# and source schemas match target schema exactly.
# So no further transformation is needed.

# Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
